newsitem.title: GERMANY: Asia must avoid rapid stainless steel expansion.
newsitem.headline: Asia must avoid rapid stainless steel expansion.

text.p: Asian capacity in stainless steel manufacturing could soon exceed regional demand as new mill projects in this growth market come on stream, Japanese trader Mitsui & Co Ltd said.
This would have a negative impact on prices of stainless steel, which accounts for two thirds of global nickel use, Mitsui's assistant general manager Mikio Sakamoto said.

In a speech delivered at a Metal Bulletin industry conference, Sakamoto said Asian consumption of cold rolled stainless steel sheet (CR) in Asia might rise to 2.53 million tonnes in the 1995-2000 period from 1.61 million in 1995.
But if planned expansions went ahead as planned, CR capacity in 2000 could already be 2.38 million tonnes compared with a mere 1.23 million in 1995.

Sakamoto said the final capacity in 2000 could easily be higher -- Indonesia by then might have twice the 125,000 tonnes per year (tpy) extra capacity implied in the current estimate and China might not have published all of its expansion plans.
In addition, the Asian market would remain subject to import penetration of up to three million tonnes a year from oversupplied markets in Europe and Japan.
Asian investors were partly ignoring these figures because they were attracted by possible returns from stainless steel sales, which are three or four times those achieved in mass (carbon) steels.
Emerging countries were viewing stainless steel as a prestigious industry reflecting growing affluence and made its development a matter of national pride.

Another reason for lacking caution was perhaps the ex-patriate Chinese business community, which was channelling resources into the industry purely on the basis of entrepreneurial optimism, Sakamoto believed.
Economically operating Japanese steel plants could be the main losers in the battle for Asian market share, he told some 250 delegates gathered here. and growing affluence.
